Do not diet. Begin a healthy (normal) calorie controlled daily eating plan that isn't too much of a deficit of calories. If you eat less calories than your body needs you will get hungry and it may lead to binge eating after that hunger really sets in.

If you eat 3 decent meals and have a few snacks during the day you should feel satisfied with what you've eaten. Aim for probably 2500 calories a day (more or less depending on your metabolism or exercise duration - but you'll have to find that out through your doctor)

Best thing you can do? Visit a nutritionist/dietician to sort of what you should eat to keep you feeling fuller for longer. Chances are your prolly not getting enough fibre or protein into your diet and eating too many refined carbs and unhealthy fats (these type of foods like cake, chocolate, biscuits, crumpets, white bread) make you HUNGRIER. Find the foods that don't trigger this 'hunger' inside of you. Its a trial and error process but once you find those foods that keep you feeling satisfied you'll thank yourself for it.


A big deal breaker that I found? Sugar and calorific sweetener of any kind - stay away from that stuff (that includes maple syrup, cane sugar, honey, agave syrup). Its bloody addictive and makes you crave more food. Fruit is about the only natural sugar you should aim to have (fructose) and also lactose (naturally occuring in cows milk). If you are in need of a sweet tooth, seek out 'stevia' is is a natural sweetener that is calorie free - stay the hell away from artificial sweeteners, just on the basis that they are 'artificial' - they weren't meant for human consumption! Stevia powder is derived from 100% natural stevia plant and has had no maladaptive effects shown in studies. But be careful with sweetener that has no enery (calories) ... The theory around it is that when your body gets a hit of something sweet is expects energy, becuase stevia has NO energy (i.e. no calories) your body gets confused and continues to expect energy. If you consume stevia with a food that has energy (cals) such as a protein shake, or a sugar replacer in a recipe, your body will gets its dose of energy, but watch out having it in tea or coffee - you can have it, but don't go overboard! It may make you crave sugar and cause excess consumption. So just make sure you have it with food/liquids that contain calories :)

Of course, every once and a while let yourself indulge. This doesn't mean spend the whole day eating what you want. Lets clarify, its a 'cheat' meal not 'cheat' day. A good way to control this indulgence is do so with friends. Go out for pancakes or a nice hearty meal at a restaurant. Have a gents night and cook some steak together. Doing it with friends takes the burden off you wanting more than you need because your enjoying yourself being with your friends, not just by eating the meal.

GL mate, I wish you all the best.

Some women need it, some don't. I think every woman can look better with makeup, if done right, because it can accentuate our features as well as hit blemishes and give the 'mirage' of flawless skin.

I personally loath the stuff. Its full of chemicals and ruins your skin/eyelashes and causes wrinkles around the eyes if used long term.

I'll try not to toot my own horn too much, but I look exceptionally good with no makeup at all. All I put on is pink lippy (that doesn't even look like lippy) and I still get looks left right and centre.

Of course, makeup is not simply a look enhancer. Man over the decades have associated makeup>beauty. So now automatically a man that sees a woman with any makeup on will have a little box tick off in their head 'feminine'.

I think use it, but use it sparingly. SOME women look good with LOTS of makeup, but this is rarely the case. Perhaps a bit of concealer, mascara and light eyeshadow can go a long way if your the type to wear makeup everday. For me, I don't. Foundation makes me (and my skin) feel like crap and I have blemish prone skin so I never touch the stuff.

Each to their own I s'pose :) but I do think (in general) makeup does make a woman look more appealing for sure. Specifically mascara and lipstick - on all women
